newsitem.title: UK: FSU beet areas moist enough, cold air coming-Licht.
newsitem.headline: FSU beet areas moist enough, cold air coming-Licht.

text.p: Sugar beet growing areas in the former Soviet Union still have more than adequate moisture but the crop could yet suffer from an expected surge of colder air across the region, statistician F.O. Licht said on Wednesday.
In its daily report Licht said beet areas were dry in the week ended October 15, which had greatly facilitated harvesting operations.
"Soil moisture levels have declined but are still rated adequate to surplus," Licht said.
"Colder air is expected to surge across the area but a prolonged freeze thaw situation, which could spoil beets, is not yet indicated," it said.
In its first estimate of the world sugar balance for the 1996/97 crop year, Licht estimated lower beet sugar production for Russia and Ukraine, eastern Europe's two largest producers.
Ukrainian output was forecast at 3.15 million tonnes raw value, down from the 3.78 million turned out in 1995/96.
Russia was expected to produce 1.82 million tonnes after a previous 2.24 million, Licht said.
